models.prompt:
Generate ONE new E.T. and Pomelo gallery artwork from the single original cat photo attached to the user's CURRENT message. Use that original photo as the ONLY image input. Do not use any earlier generated draft or repository reference image. The aesthetic is entirely described below.

SUBJECT IDENTITY: Exactly one real adult ginger-and-white short-haired cat. Preserve the cat in the reference, especially these three feature groups: (1) a full softly rounded face with substantial cheeks, slightly narrowed amber-gold eyes and the same lazy mildly unimpressed expression, a small salmon-pink triangular nose; (2) pale cream-white muzzle and chin continuing into a broad white throat/chest, orange forehead and cheeks with the original white/orange boundaries and no invented large white forehead blaze; (3) distinct ginger tabby lines on the forehead and cheeks, deeper orange bands on the forelegs, pale lower forelegs and white paw tips. Keep the sturdy adult body build, natural fur color, ear shape, and original head/face identity; do not turn it into a kitten or slim-faced different cat.

MANDATORY NEW REQUIREMENT: THE ENTIRE CAT MUST BE IN FRAME AND VISIBLE. Show the head, both ears, full neck/chest, complete long torso and back, hindquarters, both hind legs with hind paws, both front legs and front paws, and the WHOLE tail with tip. There must be no cropping of ears, paws or tail and no scenic wall or panel covering the torso or rump. The source has obscured anatomy: you are explicitly authorized to plausibly complete the hidden hindquarters, hind legs and tail consistent with this adult ginger-and-white cat's body build and visible fur patterns. These regions should be anatomically natural and unobtrusive, with no extra limbs. Use one clear continuous body silhouette and a readable natural arrangement of all four legs. Let the tail rest gently along the near side of the platform, visible from rump to tip. Use an open low platform, no box, no tall front/side/back panels or furniture concealing the cat.

THE LITTLE STORY: The cat is lounging lengthwise along a small low white display plinth, body extending toward image-left. Its chest and head are toward image-right; its cheek leans lazily against a small cream enamel radiator beside its head on the RIGHT. Its TWO FRONT LEGS hang loosely over the FRONT edge of the plinth, with the image-left front paw lower and the image-right front paw slightly higher and curling inward, matching the source's funny dangling-paw gesture. Keep the sleepy bored gaze toward the camera. Arrange the completed hind legs naturally side-on toward the left of the body, relaxed on the open plinth and separated enough to read both rear paws. Position tail in a relaxed curve in front of or beside the hindquarters, all visible and distinct from the legs. No impossible twist in the spine. The radiator only touches the cheek/side of head, never hides the torso or the forepaws.

COMPOSITION AND MINIATURE SET: Rebuild this as a complete, coherent, realistic white-studio miniature scene. A simple low rectangular matte ivory/white plinth supports the whole cat. Use a restrained slightly elevated three-quarter view, wide enough to see the entire body length, both hind legs and tail, while still showing the face clearly. A landscape frame suits the full body, with moderate white breathing room around every outer edge. A small freestanding cream enamel radiator with 3–4 rounded vertical columns and two short feet sits on the right side of the same plinth beside the cat's head. Radiator height reaches just above the cheek and ears without dominating the frame. The whole small stage sits on a seamless clean white studio floor, with its front and side edges and cast shadow establishing real physical depth and miniature scale. No large backboard, no side walls, no enclosing chair. The cat's relaxed body weight presses naturally into the plinth. The forelegs hang over its front edge and paws end just above the studio floor. Remove the original hanging clothes, household clutter, fabrics, basin and debris; build this entirely new small photographic set.

REAL PHOTOGRAPHY: Genuine individually resolved cat fur, realistic anatomy and body weight, softly reflective cream enamel radiator, subtle matte painted-wood/plaster platform surface. Softbox studio lighting with gentle shadow gradients; believable cheek-to-radiator contact shadow and slight fur compression, cat-to-plinth contact shadows, natural paws and radiator-foot shadows, and a grounded plinth-to-floor shadow. Keep face, paws and body clearly readable with moderate depth of field. The cat is photoreal with natural fur, not plastic, resin, felt, a doll, cartoon, illustration or CG toy. White cyclorama background with subtle spatial tones, no flat white erasure, no hard cutout edges, no disembodied cat sections, no floating body or props. No extra cats, duplicate limbs, clothes, accessories, text, logo, watermark, frame or printed gallery name.

Output exactly ONE finished draft preview. Do not publish.
